How can we help?

Answers to common questions about Human Atlas, and how to reach us if something isn't working.

Contact support

Report a bug, ask a question or suggest a feature. Include your device, browser and the category you were viewing so we can help faster.

Open a support request ↗

Frequently asked questions

The 3D model doesn't load or the screen stays blank.

Human Atlas needs a modern browser with WebGL enabled. Try the following:

  • Update your browser or device to the latest version.
  • Enable hardware acceleration in your browser settings.
  • Close other tabs or apps to free up memory, then reload.
  • Check your connection — the anatomy data downloads on first load.
How do I rotate, zoom and select structures?

Drag to rotate, pinch or scroll to zoom, and tap or click a structure to inspect it. Use the front, back and side buttons to reset the camera, and the search box to find a structure within the current category.

What do Isolate and Exploded view do?

Isolate hides everything except your selection so you can study it on its own. Exploded view spreads layers apart to show how structures fit together. Use Clear selection to return to the full view.

How do I see inside the heart?

Open the Heart category and use Reveal inside, or hide the heart walls layer. Chamber cavities are shown as solid volumes.

Why do some organs have only one piece?

Category counts reflect modeled pieces in the source dataset, not distinct organs. Small organs such as the stomach or spleen are a single mesh, and the data does not include detailed internal kidney anatomy.

Can I use Human Atlas for medical decisions?

No. Human Atlas is an educational tool based on an adult male reference model. It does not represent all anatomy or human variation and must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or surgical planning.

Does Human Atlas collect my personal data?

The app does not require an account. Fonts are loaded from Google Fonts; you can review Google's privacy policy for how that service handles requests.

Where does the anatomy data come from?

Models come from BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science, licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International ↗.
